function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
The debate over who’s the “greatest” basketball player ever has been going on forever—and it really depends on what you’re looking at. Here’s how most people break it down: | Category | Leading Candidates | |----------|--------------------| | **All‑time statistical dominance** | *Michael Jordan* – 30.12 PPG, 6.26 RPG, 8.56 APG; 10× All‑NBA First Team
*LeBron James* – 27.1 PPG, 7.4 RPG, 7.4 APG; 18+ seasons still playing | | **Championship success & clutch play** | *Michael Jordan* – 6 NBA titles, 6 Finals MVPs, iconic game‑winning shots
*Kobe Bryant* – 5 titles, legendary work ethic (“Mamba Mentality”)
*Tim Duncan* – 5 titles, defensive anchor | | **Longevity & consistency** | *Karl Malone* – 19 years, 20+ points per season average
*Hakeem Olajuwon* – 16 years, dominant inside presence | | **Impact on the sport globally** | *Magic Johnson*, *Larry Bird*, *Shaquille O’Neal* – each changed how the game was played and marketed | ### Why Michael Jordan often tops the list: 1. **Peak performance:** His scoring title streak, perfect shooting percentages in playoffs, and ability to dominate both ends of the floor set him apart during his prime. 2. **Cultural impact:** He turned the NBA into a global brand, created the Air Jordan line, and became synonymous with excellence. 3. **Clutch factor:** Six championships in six finals appearances—no one else has matched that level of postseason perfection. ### Why LeBron James keeps the conversation alive: 1. **Versatility:** Averaging near triple‑double numbers across multiple positions shows he can do almost anything on the court. 2. **Durability:** Over 21 seasons, he remains among the league’s top performers while staying relatively injury-free. 3. **Adaptation:** From the early 2000s to today, he evolved from a pure scorer to a masterful facilitator and defender. ### Other strong contenders: - **Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar** – Most career points, unstoppable skyhook.
- **Bill Russell** – 11 championships in 13 seasons, unmatched defensive legacy.
- **Wilt Chamberlain** – Record‑breaking single‑season averages, two‑hundred point games. --- #### Bottom Line If you weigh championship pedigree + cultural influence heavily, **Michael Jordan** usually wins out. If longevity, versatility, and sustained elite production matter more, many lean toward **LeBron James**. Ultimately, there isn’t a definitive answer—it comes down to personal criteria and era preference. What matters most is appreciating all those legends who shaped the game we love!
